h: מוֹצָאֵי יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, ח׳ Motzei Yom Kippur, 8

p: It says in the Midrash (Koheles Rabbah 9:7):
and drink your wine with a good heart,
כִּי כְבָר רָצָה הָאֱלֹהִים אֶת מַעֲשֶׂיךָ.
for God has already accepted your deeds.'"
once the first blemish has been repaired,
"In sadness shall you eat of it."
כִּי זֶהוּ עִיקַּר כֹּחַ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע
For this is the main power of the yetzer hara:
into sadness and slackness in avodah.
And once the blemish is repaired,
he will eat his bread with joy.
"And drink your wine with a good heart":
the yetzer tov and the yetzer hara,
וְלֵב טוֹב מְרַמֵּז עַל לֵב אֶחָד
while lev tov, "a good heart," alludes to one heart
that has been refined to good
for in wine too there is found
something of the mixture of good and evil,
כַּאֲמָרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה יט, ה)
"She squeezed grapes and gave it to him."
allude to the root of the words of Torah
and drink of the wine I have mixed."
And this is "your bread" and "your wine":
that is, the root of the words of Torah
that belong to each soul according to its root,
כִּדְאִיתָא מֵהַבַּעַל שֵׁם טוֹב זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
as is brought from the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory,
כִּי כְבָר רָצָה הָאֱלֹהִים אֶת מַעֲשֶׂיךָ
"For God has already accepted your deeds."
כִּי אִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כ, ד)
For it says in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 20:4)
and in the Pesikta (Pesikta deRav Kahana 26:4)
That is, they expounded the word chafar
"and let them search out the land for us,"
וְכֵן הוּא מְפוֹרָשׁ בַּפְּסִיקְתָּא (פְּסִיקְתָּא רַבָּתִי מז, א)
and so it is explicit in the Pesikta (Pesikta Rabbasi 47:1),
that it means to scout and to spy,
And this is the refining of the good
that belong to each soul according to its root,
וְזֶהוּ כִּי כְבָר רָצָה הָאֱלֹהִים אֶת מַעֲשֶׂיךָ
And this is "for God has already accepted your deeds":
in the holy eating of the whole year.
